title: Square Enix 否认私有化计划，相关报道曾致股价大涨
content:
Square Enix denies going private after report sends stock surging | GamesIndustry.biz

.
Square Enix has issued a statement denying it is exploring taking the company private after a report in Japanese business magazine Sentaku
claimed
the publisher had drawn interest from foreign investment funds.
"The September issue of the monthly magazine Sentaku carried a report regarding the possibility of Square Enix Holdings Co., Ltd. (the 'Company') going private," the company wrote in a succinct
statement
. "However, this information was not announced by the Company.
"No consideration is currently being given within the Company to taking the Company private."
The Sentaku report sent Square Enix's stock surging on the Tokyo Stock Exchange, rising as much as 8.3 percent throughout the day, according to
Investing.com
(thanks,
Eurogamer
).
Activist investor 3D Investment Partners, which holds roughly 18.5 percent of Square Enix's shares, allegedly sparked this speculation. It
has previously pushed the company's board to reassess its strategy
.
Square Enix has spent the past four years restructuring, selling Western studios Crystal Dynamics, Eidos Montreal, and Square Enix Montreal to Embracer Group in 2022, then
laying off more than 100 staff across the US and UK in 2025
as part of a consolidation of development in Japan.
A take-private deal would require buying back all outstanding shares at a premium. Saudi Arabia's Public Investment Fund took a similar path with its
acquisition of Electronic Arts
, a deal that left EA in billions of dollars in debt.
Square Enix reported strong first-quarter growth earlier this month
, with profit rising 175.5% to ¥13.2 billion ($82.9 million). The company attributed these results to its Digital Entertainment segment, which saw high sales in HD Games, MMO, and Smart Devices/PC Browser sub-segments.
